title: Queen's Gambit Declined: the Exchange Variation and its plans
outcomes: Names the pawn structure that arises by move 7 in the Exchange Variation (White: d4 and e3 and no c-pawn; Black: c6 and d5 and no e-pawn) and the order of moves that reaches it
Starts the minority attack with b4 only after counting what attacks and defends the pawn, and checks what the opponent's last move attacks before carrying on with any plan
Chooses between two exchange offers for Black by checking them, not by the idea alone
Sees that a plan in the centre or on the kingside (Ne5, f4) can be as good as the minority attack, instead of treating one plan as the only one

steps.text: **Queen's Gambit Declined** (ECO D30): 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6. In our online data (4,752,291 games, September 2026) 63,292 games reach this position, and 6,259 reach the position named the *Exchange Variation*, after 3.Nc3 Nf6 4.cxd5. This lesson follows the Exchange Variation, where both sides have clear plans to test. Its pawn structure (White d4 and e3, Black c6 and d5, no e-pawn) is close to the one in the Carlsbad lesson, but not identical: here Black has no e-pawn.

steps.caption: Position after 1.d4 d5 2.c4 e6, White to move. Step through one line of the Exchange Variation. Other moves are possible; this line shows how the structure arises.

line.say: Nc3 puts a knight on c3, where it attacks d5.
Nf6 develops a knight and defends d5.
White exchanges on d5: the c-pawn for Black's d-pawn.
Black retakes with the e-pawn. White now has no c-pawn and Black has no e-pawn.
Bg5 attacks the knight on f6.
Be7 defends the knight on f6.
e3 supports the pawn on d4. White now has pawns on d4 and e3.
c6 supports the pawn on d5. Black now has pawns on c6 and d5.
Bd3 aims the bishop along the diagonal to h7.
Nbd7 develops the last knight and defends f6.
Qc2 defends the bishop on d3.
Black castles kingside. Both sides now have the pieces for the plans on the next steps.

claims.statement: After Nc3 the knight attacks d5.
After Nf6 the knight defends d5.
After cxd5 exd5 no file is open; the c-file is half-open for White and the e-file for Black.
After Bg5 the bishop attacks f6.
After Be7 the bishop defends f6.
After c6 the pawn on c6 defends d5.
After Bd3 the bishop attacks h7 along an open diagonal.
After Nbd7 the knight defends f6.
After Qc2 the queen defends d3.
After O-O the black king is on the kingside.
White has 3 pawns on the queenside (files a to d): a2, b2 and d4.
Black has 4 pawns on the queenside (files a to d): a7, b7, c6 and d5.

steps.text: **What strong players chose** (results of games, not evaluations). Source: our masters data, 329,379 games, both players rated 2500 or more. After 3.Nc3 Nf6, White played 4.cxd5 in 4,184 of 5,794 games (Bg5: 813, Nf3: 739). Of those 4,184 games White won 1,493, 1,700 were drawn and Black won 991. After 8...O-O, White played Nf3 in 53 games and Nge2 in 36. Samples are small; results also reflect the players.

**When the minority attack fits (rule of thumb).** White has two pawns against three on the a-, b- and c-files, the pawn pushed to b4 can be supported (here the rook on b1 defends it), and Black has no quicker threat. It does not fit when something of yours is attacked. Ask first: what did my opponent's last move attack? The next item shows what skipping that question costs.

**Black's side (rule of thumb).** Black often looks to exchange minor pieces, for example a knight against a bishop that has come to g5 or g3. Condition: the exchange must be safe in the position in front of you. In the next item two knight moves both attack the bishop, and the engine rates them very differently. Check the move, not just the idea.

steps.title: One piece moves, the plan flips
steps.prompt: In all three positions White considers b4. Predict for each whether it is reasonable, then check. The first two differ only in where Black's knight stands (g6 or e6). The third differs from the first only in where White's knight stands (f3 or e2).
Think about the positions you played without hints. Before you chose a move, what did you check? Write one line for each side.

fields.label: As White: what I checked before pushing a pawn
As Black: what I checked before offering an exchange
